mainTopic: When does הפקר leave the owner? רבי אבא's question from vows, רבא's challenge from a שכיב מרע and his new reason (the גזירה of בית חורון), and a ברייתא about taking back הפקר within three days
overview: The גמרא is testing רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי יוסי: something made הפקר still belongs to its owner until someone actually picks it up. רבי אבא asks a question from a ברייתא about vows. If the owner made his food הפקר before he vowed, the other person may eat it, so why should the order matter if the owner still owns it? רבי אבא answers his own question: a person who vows does not have in mind what he already made הפקר. Then רבא challenges רבי יוחנן from a שכיב מרע (dying man). He gave part of his property to one person and all the rest to another, and the second gift counts as "everything" only if the first gift had already left him. Because of this, רבא gives a new reason for רבי יוסי: it is a rabbinic decree (גזירה) because of the gift of בית חורון, where a gift was used as a trick to get around a vow. Finally, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that someone who makes his field הפקר can take it back for three days, and the discussion of this source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the order of the vow and the הפקר matter?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the owner made the food הפקר before his vow, the food is permitted. רבי אבא asks: if הפקר stays with the owner until someone takes it, why does the order matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he made it ownerless before he made his vow, it is permitted. Now, if you say it stays his until it reaches the person who acquires it, what difference does it make whether the vow came first or the הפקר came first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about a person who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from someone else's food. Then it uses that ruling to challenge the idea that הפקר stays with the owner until someone takes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the order matters. If the vow came first, the food is forbidden. If the הפקר came first, the food is allowed. But according to רבי יוחנן's reading of רבי יוסי, the food is still the owner's in both cases until someone picks it up, so the other person would be getting benefit from the owner either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Declaring something ownerless, so that anyone may take it
A vow, here one that forbids getting benefit from a certain person
The possession of the one who acquires the item
What difference does it make? A phrase used to argue that two cases should be the same

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה הֶפְקֵירוֹ קוֹדֵם לְנִדְרוֹ —
phrases.english: But if his declaring it ownerless came before his vow,
it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עַד דְּאָתֵי לִרְשׁוּת זוֹכֶה,
phrases.english: And if you say it stays his until it comes into the possession of the one who acquires it,
what difference does it make to me if his vow came before his declaring it ownerless,
or if his declaring it ownerless came before his vow?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עַד דְּאָתֵי לִרְשׁוּת זוֹכֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that רבי אבא was quoting and draws out his challenge from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי יוסי: הפקר does not leave the owner until someone acquires it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the item stays the owner's in both cases, the order of the vow and the הפקר should make no difference. Yet the ברייתא does make a difference.

steps.title: A person who vows does not mean to include what he already made הפקר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers his own question. The difference comes from what the person meant when he vowed, not from the rules of הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked the question and he answered it: anyone who makes a vow does not have in mind what he has already made ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The same person who asked the question now answers it. He explains that the difference between the two cases comes from what the person intended when he vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer leaves רבי יוחנן's rule about הפקר in place. Instead, it explains the ברייתא through the person's intent. When he vows after making the food הפקר, he does not mean for his vow to cover food he already gave up, so the vow never takes hold on it.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְשַׁנֵּי לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection, and he himself answered it
The one who makes a vow
His intention, what he has in mind

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְשַׁנֵּי לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he answered it:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבא, the same one who asked the question.

phrases.english: Anyone who makes a vow does not have in mind
what he has already made ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְשַׁנֵּי לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the reason for the difference from the rules of הפקר to what the person meant when he vowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order matters only if הפקר takes effect right away, so the ברייתא would go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order matters because the vow was never meant to include food that was already made הפקר. So רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about vows does not disprove רבי יוחנן, because a person's vow does not cover what he already made הפקר.

steps.title: רבא challenges from a dying man who gave part to one person and all to another
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a case of a שכיב מרע (dying man). He gave part of his property to the first person and all the rest to the second, and then he recovered. The first person acquires, but the second does not. This seems to show that a gift leaves the giver before the receiver takes hold of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection: if a dying man gave part of his property to the first person and all the rest to the second, the first person acquired it and the second did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new source to challenge רבי יוחנן's idea that something stays with the owner until the new person acquires it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second person did not acquire because he received "everything," and a dying man who gives away everything can take it back if he recovers. But it only counts as "everything" if the part given to the first person had already left the giver. That suggests property leaves the giver even before it reaches the receiver, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of them, meaning part of the property
All of them, meaning all the remaining property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The first got only part of the property, and that gift holds. The second got "all the rest," and that gift does not hold if the giver recovers.

phrases.english: רבא raised an objection:
If a dying man gave part of his property to the first person and all the rest to the second,
phrases.notes: This is about a שכיב מרע who gave his property away and then recovered.

phrases.english: the first person acquired it,
the second person did not acquire it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אבא's question was answered, רבא raises a new challenge to the same idea from a different area of law, gifts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a gift or הפקר does not leave the owner until it reaches the one who acquires it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gift to the second person counts as "everything" only if the first person's share had already left the giver. So property leaves the giver before the receiver acquires it.

steps.title: רבא gives a new reason: a rabbinic decree because of the gift of בית חורון
steps.stepSummary: Since his challenge undercut רבי יוחנן's explanation, רבא gives his own reason. He says רבי יוסי's ruling is a גזירה, made because of the case of the gift of בית חורון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: this is the reason for רבי יוסי's ruling. It is a rabbinic decree because of the gift of בית חורון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's case of the שכיב מרע made it hard to accept רבי יוחנן's idea that הפקר stays with the owner until someone takes it. So רבא now gives a completely different reason for רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that רבי יוחנן's ownership-based explanation of רבי יוסי is being set aside. The reason is no longer about who owns the food. The חכמים made a decree because declaring הפקר could be used as a trick to let the forbidden person benefit, just like the trick gift in בית חורון.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier explanation is being dropped.
A rabbinic decree, made to prevent a problem
The gift of בית חורון, a known case where a gift was used as a trick to get around a vow

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוסי's ruling still rests on the food belonging to the owner, as רבי יוחנן explained it. According to רבא, the ban comes from a rabbinic decree against tricks, not from the rules of ownership.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole basis of רבי יוסי's ruling. The ruling no longer tells us anything about when הפקר leaves the owner's hands.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Yosei:
It is a decree because of the gift of Beit Choron.
phrases.notes: This story comes in a משנה later in נדרים: someone gave a gift just to get around a vow, and the חכמים didn't allow it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised by the שכיב מרע case in step 3 by giving a new reason for רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason: a rabbinic decree instead of a rule about ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי forbids the food because הפקר stays with the owner until someone takes it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי forbids it as a גזירה, so that people do not use הפקר as a trick to get around a vow, as happened with the gift of בית חורון.

steps.title: A ברייתא: one can take back a declaration of ownerlessness for three days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who makes his field הפקר can take it back for three days, but not after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: if someone makes his field הפקר, for all three days he can take it back. From then on, he cannot take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about הפקר. This sets up the next discussion about how this source fits the views on הפקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a declaration of הפקר is not fully final right away. For three days the owner can still change his mind, and after that it is final. This new point about how long הפקר takes to become final will be discussed next.

phrases.english: It is taught: one who declares his field ownerless,
for all three days
he is able to take it back;
from here onward,
phrases.notes: He means after the three days are over.

phrases.english: he is not able to take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about הפקר, setting up further discussion of how and when הפקר takes effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who makes his field הפקר can take it back within three days. After three days he cannot.
